title: Microsoft Teams: add SharePoint agents to chats from the in-context store
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap, Microsoft's tenant notice and the cited documentation. Its licensing, billing and shared-chat permissions statements are accurate, and it clearly distinguishes general Teams controls from controls confirmed for this feature.

claims.claim: Users can discover and add SharePoint agents directly within Teams chats on Desktop and Mac.
claims.quote: With this release, users can discover and add SharePoint agents directly within Microsoft Teams chats on Desktop and Mac.

claims.claim: Add Agents and Bots in the chat roster dropdown opens an in-context store for agent discovery and selection.
claims.quote: Agents can be added via the Add Agents and Bots option in the chat roster dropdown, which opens the in-context store for discovery and selection.

claims.claim: SharePoint agents appear in the Teams Store under the Agents category.
claims.quote: SharePoint agents will be available in the Teams Store under the Agents category.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Why it matters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Mixed licensing accurately describes access through Copilot licensing or pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: You can manage who can access agents through Copilot license assignment. Or, if your organization has the pay-as-you-go billing set up, you can control who can access agents through the security groups assigned to the billing policy.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice asks for intended users to have E3 or E5 licensing with Teams.
claims.quote: Ensure that intended users have E3 or E5 (with Teams) licensing

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The notice additionally names a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence or pay-as-you-go separately set up for SharePoint agents on Mac.
claims.quote: one of the following options: - Microsoft 365 Copilot license OR- Pay-as-you-go (PAYG) separately setup for SharePoint agents on MAC.

claims.claim: SharePoint-agent responses respect the requesting user's permissions on their data sources.
claims.quote: if a user has access to the agent but not to the site or document library it references, the agent's responses for this user don't include content from those restricted sources.

claims.claim: If some chat members cannot access an answer that the requester can access, the requester is told it cannot be automatically added to the chat.
claims.quote: If the user who asks the question has permission to see the answer, but some members in the chat group don't, the user sees a message explaining that the answer can't be automatically added to the chat.

claims.claim: Restricted content discovery hides the Agent icon on the flagged site.
claims.quote: Once you flag a site with restricted content discovery, users can't see the Agent icon on the global header of the site.

claims.claim: Restricted content discovery prevents content from the flagged site being added to other agents.
claims.quote: they don't have access to use the ready-made agent, create new agents, or add content from that site to any other agents.

claims.claim: Permissions on the .agent file determine who can access or edit the agent.
claims.quote: The permissions on the `.agent` file determine who can access or edit the agent.

claims.claim: The notice describes adding agents to conversations for collaboration without describing additional agent actions.
claims.quote: This enables users to quickly bring SharePoint agents into conversations to support collaboration.

claims.claim: Additional actions specific to agents added through this in-context-store feature are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents Teams actions Add Agents and Bots; SharePoint agents Teams in-context store controls actions. Read Manage access to agents in SharePoint, Share an agent from SharePoint in Teams and Share an agent in Microsoft Teams; none describes additional actions specific to this store.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The SharePoint-agent blocking control described in Microsoft 365 admin center currently affects Copilot Chat, not Teams.
claims.quote: Currently, blocking an agent only affects its availability in Copilot Chat. It doesn't yet apply to OneDrive, SharePoint, or Teams.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Administrators can manage SharePoint-agent access through Copilot licence assignment.
claims.quote: You can manage who can access agents through Copilot license assignment.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: For pay-as-you-go, only users in the security group assigned to the billing policy have agent access.
claims.quote: Only users in the security group assigned to the billing policy have access to agents.

claims.claim: The SharePoint-agent Azure billing resource is used whenever a user without a Microsoft Copilot licence uses a SharePoint agent.
claims.quote: That resource is used whenever a user without a Microsoft Copilot license uses a SharePoint agent.

claims.claim: A SharePoint-agent interaction uses 12 messages to respond to a single complex prompt.
claims.quote: each interaction with a SharePoint agent uses 12 messages (10 messages for tenant graph grounding, and 2 messages for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from the user.

claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding accounts for 10 messages in that interaction.
claims.quote: 10 messages for tenant graph grounding

claims.claim: Generative answers account for 2 messages in that interaction.
claims.quote: 2 messages for generative answers

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Governance guidance
claims.claim: SharePoint-agent usage charges appear under the Copilot Studio meter on the invoice.
claims.quote: Charges of SharePoint agent usage appear under the Copilot Studio meter in your invoice.

claims.claim: Interactive use by authenticated Microsoft Copilot users in Microsoft 365 apps and services is included at no extra cost.
claims.quote: Interactive use of generative answers, tenant graph grounding and agent actions by authenticated Microsoft Copilot users, in Microsoft 365 apps and services, are included at no extra cost.

claims.claim: A budget can be created in Microsoft Cost Management under Monitoring > Budgets.
claims.quote: You can quickly create a budget under **Monitoring** > **Budgets** for your selected scope.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes a price of USD $0.01 per message for agents in SharePoint.
claims.quote:
| Service | What's Counted? | What's billed? (USD) |
| Agents in SharePoint | The number of messages used. | $0.01/message |

claims.claim: Learn lists SharePoint administrator as a prerequisite role for setting up SharePoint agents as an Azure billing resource.
claims.quote:
To set up SharePoint agents as a resource in Azure, you need to have at least the following permissions as:
- A SharePoint administrator

claims.claim: Setting up the SharePoint-agent Azure resource requires Owner or Contributor access to the Azure subscription.
claims.quote: Owner or Contributor Azure roles to an Azure subscription

claims.claim: The setup also requires Owner or Contributor access to a resource group linked to that subscription.
claims.quote: Owner or Contributor Azure roles to an Azure resource group linked to the same Azure subscription

claims.claim: The Azure Owner or Contributor roles are needed during billing setup.
claims.quote: You only need the Owner or Contributor Azure roles during the billing setup process.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The general tenant-level Teams control is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Teams admin center and access **Teams apps** > **Manage apps**.
2. Select the app on the **Manage apps** page and select **Allow** or **Block** option.

claims.claim: The MicrosoftTeams module documents Update-M365TeamsApp with -Id and Boolean -IsBlocked to modify app state.
claims.quote: PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference describes its -IsBlocked $true example as unblocking, making that example unreliable guidance for a blocking command.
claims.quote:
PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not specifically confirm Manage apps applicability to SharePoint agents discovered through the in-context store.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents Teams admin center Manage apps; SharePoint agents in-context Teams. Read learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-apps and learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint; no store-specific applicability statement found.

claims.claim: Teams Administrator is the role Learn names for using Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.claim: Admins can turn Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint on or off per user through the Copilot licence's service plans in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Under the license details page for Microsoft Copilot on the Microsoft 365 admin center, admins can turn 'Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint' on or off on a per-user basis.

claims.claim: Turning off that service plan also disables Copilot in OneDrive for the user.
claims.quote: However, this change also disables Copilot in OneDrive and on the SharePoint page authoring Copilot for that user.

claims.claim: Turning off that service plan also disables SharePoint page-authoring Copilot for the user.
claims.quote: However, this change also disables Copilot in OneDrive and on the SharePoint page authoring Copilot for that user.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice recommends briefing helpdesk staff about access to and use of SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: Inform helpdesk staff in case users have questions about accessing or using SharePoint agents.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page specifically documenting this in-context-store capability was found.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents in-context Teams; SharePoint agents Teams in-context store Add agents and bots controls actions. Read Manage access to agents in SharePoint, manage-apps and training/Share an agent in Microsoft Teams; these cover surrounding features, not the roster store.

claims.claim: Restricted content discovery can turn off agent-related features on individual SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: As a SharePoint admin, you can turn off all agent-related features on individual sites by using the restricted content discovery feature.

claims.claim: Microsoft Cost Management provides consumption details for SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: in Microsoft cost management, you can see a detailed breakdown by feature, including SharePoint agents.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice identifies all Teams users on Desktop and Mac as affected.
claims.quote: Who is affected: All users of Microsoft Teams on Desktop and Mac.
